name: The Chaldeans who accused the Jews
charge: Informing against the Jews to have them cast into the furnace for keeping the second commandment
summary: Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, reciting the king's own decree back to him and naming the three men who would not bow. They did not come for an offense against themselves; they came because Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego kept the commandment, and the decree made that a capital matter.
offense: At that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews. They rehearsed the decree to Nebuchadnezzar — every man that shall hear the sound of the cornet shall fall down and worship the golden image, and whoso falleth not down shall be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace — and then laid the charge: There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up. Envy of men set over the province, dressed as loyalty to the king.
judgment: The account records no personal punishment upon these accusers. The men killed by the furnace were those who carried the three bound servants into it; they are not identified as the Chaldeans who brought the accusation (Daniel 3:22). The accused emerged unharmed. Nebuchadnezzar blessed their God, declared that no other god could deliver in this manner, and promoted them (Daniel 3:28-30). The accusation succeeded in bringing them before the furnace but failed to accomplish their destruction. The king's public acknowledgment reversed the disgrace the charge had sought to fasten upon their refusal.
offenseFull: Certain Chaldeans approached the king with an accusation against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They repeated the command to worship the image and its penalty, then named the Jewish officers as men who disregarded the king and did not serve his gods (Daniel 3:8-12).

The charge made refusal of idolatry appear as disloyalty in office. The men had indeed refused the worship, but the king's decree could not make that worship righteous. The accusers invoked public authority to bring faithful servants under a sentence of death.

verses.text: Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews.
They spake and said to the king Nebuchadnezzar, O king, live for ever.

Thou, O king, hast made a decree, that every man that shall hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, shall fall down and worship the golden image:
And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth, that he should be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his visage was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego: therefore he spake, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more than it was wont to be heated.
And he commanded the most mighty men that were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in their coats, their hosen, and their hats, and their other garments, and were cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
Therefore because the king’s commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceeding hot, the flame of the fire slew those men that took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spake, and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and come hither. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, came forth of the midst of the fire.

And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king’s counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.

Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.

Therefore I make a decree, That every people, nation, and language, which speak any thing amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill: because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort.
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, in the province of Babylon.

And the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions had the mastery of them, and brake all their bones in pieces or ever they came at the bottom of the den.
Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;

entries.commentary: Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, threescore cubits high and six cubits broad, and set it up in the plain of Dura, then gathered the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counsellors, sheriffs, and rulers to its dedication. We have seen things like this before. When they build a monument or a new federal building they hold a dedication and a ribbon-cutting ceremony. This is very similar.

A herald cried that when the people heard the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of music they were to fall down and worship the golden image. We see the same thing today when they play the national anthem at ball games and ceremonies. You are supposed to take your hat off and put your hand over your heart. That is a form of worshipping the image of the eagle today.

Whoever did not fall down and worship would the same hour be cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace, so when the music sounded all the people, nations, and languages fell down and worshipped the golden image.

Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, telling the king that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom he had set over the affairs of the province, did not regard him, serve his gods, nor worship the golden image. The reason we did not bow was according to the law. -

In his rage Nebuchadnezzar brought the three men and demanded whether they would fall down and worship, threatening the furnace and asking, who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands. He is talking tough, talking big, challenging our God when he asks who is going to deliver you out of his hands.

The three answered that they were not careful to answer him in this matter: their God whom they serve is able to deliver them from the burning fiery furnace and out of the king's hand. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that they would not serve his gods nor worship the golden image. This is exactly what was read in [Exodus 20](/bible/exodus/20).

Full of fury, Nebuchadnezzar commanded the furnace heated seven times more than usual and had his mighty men bind the three in their coats and garments and cast them in. The furnace was so hot that the flame slew the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to it. For more of this history the Song of the Three Holy Children can be read; for the sake of time it was only referenced here.

The three men fell down bound into the furnace, but Nebuchadnezzar rose up astonished and said he saw four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, unhurt, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God.

Nebuchadnezzar called them servants of the Most High God to come forth, and the fire had no power on their bodies: not a hair singed, their coats unchanged, nor the smell of fire on them. It was as if they had never fallen into the fire; not even the smell of smoke was on these brothers.

Nebuchadnezzar blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel to deliver the servants that trusted in him and would not serve nor worship any god except their own God. He understood at that time that we had our own God. Why do people not understand that today. He decreed that any people, nation, or language that spake amiss against their God would be cut in pieces, because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort, and he promoted the three in the province of Babylon. When the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the real, true, living God; other heathen rulers came to the same acknowledgement, such as Antiochus and Naaman the Syrian. -

It pleased Darius to set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, of whom Daniel was first, so the king should have no damage. Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. He was set in a very high position in government.

The presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom but could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him. He was blameless. This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God. -

The presidents and princes assembled and persuaded Darius to sign a firm decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the unchanging law of the Medes and Persians.

When Daniel knew the writing was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem kneeled and prayed three times a day, giving thanks as he did before. The men assembled, found him praying, and reported to the king that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor the decree but made his petition three times a day. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God.

The king was displeased with himself and laboured till sundown to deliver Daniel, but the men pressed that the law could not be changed, so he commanded Daniel cast into the den, saying, thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee. The king already understood why he was under the realm of Babylon and had seen what was going on. A stone was laid on the den and sealed with the king's signet.

The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, with no instruments of music brought before him and his sleep gone from him. Why would the king be fasting. He rose very early and went in haste to the den, crying with a lamentable voice, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions.

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths because innocency was found in him and he had done no hurt. The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom. -

Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages that in every dominion men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, stedfast for ever, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and who delivereth and rescueth and worketh signs and wonders. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. He had a wise and humble spirit, was beloved by the king, could answer visions and interpret dreams, and was of the king's seed as shown in chapter one. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.
